extracted.intended_audience: working men; general Victorian readers interested in social reform
extracted.subtask_description: A public address advising working-class listeners how to use newly obtained political power wisely, urging prudence, education, order, and responsible collective action. It combines moral counsel with practical recommendations for unions and political choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid flattery and empty complimenting
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Whenever a speaker, whether he is one of ourselves or not, wastes our time in boasting or flattery, I say, let us hiss him.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speakers and leaders should not be received for mere complimenting; listen for substantive truth rather than praise. Hissing is recommended for platform swaggerers who bring nothing but bluster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin with self-knowledge and humility
rubrics_metrics.description: Working men should acknowledge that 'as a body we are neither very wise nor very virtuous.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject the pretence of moral superiority; self-knowledge is the 'beginning of wisdom' and guards against rashness in political action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge leaders by knowledge, ability, and honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Use this test for would-be leaders: 'Have they anything to offer us besides indignant talk? ... Can they explain to us any reasonable, fair, safe way of getting it?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer leaders who present concrete, practicable methods over those who only stir indignation; demand explanations of how proposals will work in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use indignation but pair it with rationality and skill
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Indignation is a fine war-horse, but the war-horse must be ridden by a man: it must be ridden by rationality, skill, courage...taking definite aim.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage vigorous feeling against injustice but insist it be directed by thought, method, and appropriate means rather than mere passion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider long-term consequences before acting
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid hasty wresting of measures that 'seem to promise an immediate partial relief' because their effects may be difficult to undo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that many national evils are 'a tangled business' needing patient, well-judged processes rather than sudden fixes; weigh intergenerational consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform class interests into class functions/duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not seek to abolish class distinctions wholesale but 'turn class interests into class functions or duties' so each class performs its work under responsibility to the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for institutions where class roles express duties to the common good; change class character through knowledge and fellow-feeling rather than violent overturn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve public order and obedience to law
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The fundamental duty of a government is to preserve order, to enforce obedience of the laws.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat preservation of order as essential; disorder undermines legitimate demands and risks civil calamity. Guardians of order should include the sober poor as well as the rich.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid disorder as a political tactic
rubrics_metrics.description: Disorder will 'choke' demands and lead to loss of public sympathy and possible violent suppression ('guns that will sweep us down').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political action should avoid tactics that provoke broad public alarm or justify repression; peaceful, lawful pressure is strategically wiser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer gradual, well-prepared change to destructive haste
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Day will not break the sooner because we get up before the twilight.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use forceful destruction (a Hercules with a besom) where careful, patient reform is required; ill-prepared upheaval may make things worse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect the 'treasure of knowledge' and cultural inheritance
rubrics_metrics.description: Value 'knowledge, science, poetry, refinement of thought, feeling, and manners' as a common estate that must be guarded even while pursuing social justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware reforms that drive away or debase the classes and institutions that preserve intellectual and cultural life; balance redistribution with protection of cultural capital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote education and rescue children from labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Unions and working men should 'demand that [members] send their children to school' and not 'turn their little ones of tender age into bread-winners.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make schooling and parental responsibility enforceable aspects of co-operation; treat prevention of child labor as a central union/public duty akin to sanitary regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use co-operation to set mutual rules and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-operation creates 'rules of fellowship'—members must 'make such and such a contribution' and renounce separate advantages for common benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize unions so membership requires concrete duties (e.g., contributions, parental duties) that strengthen common good and mutual accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose representatives whose words contain methods (practical remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for men whose words 'carry that sort of kernel'—a method or plan by which an evil may be assuaged (example: Ambrose Paré's 'Tie up the arteries!').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor candidates who propose clear, actionable remedies rather than mere denunciation or rhetoric; method-mindedness indicates likely effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance resistance to oppression with sober means
rubrics_metrics.description: 'We are determined to resist oppression. But let us...show that we can keep sane in our resistance, and shape our means more and more reasonably toward the least harmful, and therefore the speediest, attainment of our end.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain moral firmness against injustice while selecting the least harmful, most effective tactics—avoid letting resistance become ferocity or madness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise personal virtues of industry, sobriety, and fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'wise man' and 'every clever workman' knows an article's value comes from invention/plan, good material, and 'skilful and honest work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate habits—industry, sobriety, faithfulness, temperance—that make the working class fit to use political power responsibly and to claim cultural benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider society as an interdependent body when judging reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Society 'stands before us like that wonderful piece of life, the human body,' with many parts whose changes affect the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid single-class solutions that ignore interdependence; reforms must account for effects across institutions, commerce, knowledge, and infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish evils removable by energy from those requiring patience
rubrics_metrics.description: 'To discern between the evils that energy can remove and the evils that patience must bear, makes the difference between manliness and childishness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize efforts where action can realistically improve conditions and accept patience where slow, structural processes govern change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch one another and enforce internal standards
rubrics_metrics.description: While watching public men, 'let us watch one another as to this duty' (e.g., parental responsibilities), imposing sanctions within the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal social pressure and union rules to enforce conduct that protects the common estate (education, sanitation, mutual support) rather than external condemnation alone.
